artifacts.summary: Implemented the per-repo orchestration queue: six additive task-lock.sh subcommands, archive-on-finish, session_liveness()-consuming liveness, and a blocking queue-check admission gate wired into /orchestrate.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a per-repo orchestration queue as six additive task-lock.sh subcommands (queue-register/heartbeat/finish/reap/list/check), built on the existing session registry: per-orchestration identity distinct from session_id, lifecycle registered->running->finished->archived, archive-on-finish rather than rm -f, liveness computed via the existing session_liveness() unchanged, and a blocking queue-check admission gate wired into /orchestrate's pre-dispatch stage. Documented in a new Orchestration-Queue CLI section in task-lock.md and two new Class Table rows in orchestrator-runtime-files.md, covered by a 17-case fixture suite, with shellcheck clean and the deployed tree fresh.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan's final phase declares Verification Tier: full but the dispatch file carries a Batch Gate Deferral section, discharge that phase by running a scoped narrowing (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow plus a suite-selection-lib.sh-resolved --only run covering every touched file) instead of the unscoped full gate 8 battery, and record the deferral explicitly in the phase's own verification notes. An independent attempt at the full unscoped battery hit a 1500s timeout, confirming the deferral is the correct call rather than merely convenient.

When adding a new identity-bearing registry record built on an existing session/task registry (e.g. a per-orchestration queue atop a session registry), reuse the existing liveness computation function verbatim by keeping the new record's pid/pid_source/heartbeat_at field names byte-identical to the existing registry's -- this lets one shared liveness function serve two independent registries with zero second transcription, which is both less code and keeps the liveness semantics provably identical across both.

A per-file context-budget ceiling (gate 20 in verify-deploy.sh) that already carries a razor-thin margin (single-digit bytes) will be pushed over by almost any genuine new mechanism's documentation, even after aggressive compaction to pointer form. The established remedy in this codebase is a 'reviewed, dated ceiling move' recorded in context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json's own derivation history (never silently bumped, never left undocumented) -- round up to the next 500B, append a dated entry explaining why the addition is necessary/non-duplicative rather than restatable bloat, and never delete prior history entries.
